points.description: States that a pointer is a variable (a named storage location that holds a value).

States that the value it holds is the memory address of another variable (or of where that data is stored). Equivalent wording such as 'refers to / points to the location of another variable in memory' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable, in any equivalent wording. Part marks: says it is a variable but does not say it holds an address (2), or says it holds or refers to a memory address but does not call it a variable (3). No marks: unrelated definitions.
